VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | FIND: `scan_health()` misreports tool availability not only for missing binaries but also for timed-out tools. `_run_tool()` returns `CompletedProcess(..., returncode=-1, stderr="TIMEOUT")` on timeout, and each runner only special-cases `"NOT_FOUND"`. When a timeout happens, the runner usually returns `[]` after parse failure, so `scan_health()` still executes the runner successfully and sets `tools_available[tool_name] = True`. FOLLOW: The insect brain receives a health report claiming the tool is available and healthy when the tool never completed. That makes timeout-induced blindness indistinguishable from a clean scan, suppresses operational signals, and can mislead reviewers into trusting empty diagnostics. FIX: Use the same availability/error propagation path for timeout as for not-found: have runners surface an execution-status flag or inspect `_run_tool` return state in `scan_health()` and set availability false for both `NOT_FOUND` and `TIMEOUT`.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | FIND: Timeout handling also breaks fix evaluation, not just health scans. `_count_tool_issues()` calls `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit`; when `_run_tool()` times out, those runners return `[]`, so `_count_tool_issues()` counts zero issues. In `evaluate_fix()`, both pre-fix and post-fix counts can therefore collapse to zero under timeout. FOLLOW: A fix can be labeled `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` because the analysis tools failed to run, not because the patch is safe. This crosses the interface into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL results mark findings `verified=True`, activating the bug-closed gate and suppressing future reports of the same bug. That is silently wrong and high severity for the PoC. FIX: Make timeout/unavailable tool runs propagate as unevaluable state into `FixEvaluation` rather than zero counts; if any required analyzer times out or is unavailable during fix evaluation, return `UNEVALUABLE` instead of computing net deltas from empty diagnostic lists.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.92
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not actually sandbox tests against the patched code when `test_cmd` references the original source tree. The function writes only the target file to a temp directory (`patched_path = tmpdir/basename(target_path)`) and then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`, but it does not rewrite command arguments, copy the repository/package layout, or ensure imports resolve to the patched file. In the active caller from `immune_agents.py`, `test_cmd` is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; from `tmpdir`, `bench/tests/` usually does not exist, and even if tests are found via absolute paths they will import the real `bench/...` modules from the original tree, not the patched temp file. Evidence in endocrine.py: only one file is copied; package directories and sibling modules are not.
FOLLOW: This defeats the module’s key advertised capability: “sandbox-test proposed fixes (no source modification).” Downstream, `FixEvaluation.tests_passed` can become false for path reasons unrelated to the patch, or true while exercising the unmodified production source instead of the patched sandbox. That propagates to `_compute_fix_verdict()`, then to `evaluate_fixes()`, then into `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()`, where SAFE/NEUTRAL can mark a finding `verified=True`. The result is either false harmful verdicts that block good fixes or false safe verdicts that close bugs without testing the patch. Both are silently wrong and directly affect end-to-end review output.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the minimal source tree rooted at the target file’s package/repo-relative path into the temp directory, write the patched file at the same relative path inside that copied tree, and run `test_cmd` against that sandbox tree (same relative paths, `cwd=tmpdir`). Do not run tests if the referenced paths are absent in the sandbox; mark the evaluation `UNEVALUABLE` instead.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a patch as `SAFE` even when it introduces new issues in one tool, as long as enough issues disappear in another. The code sums net counts across tools: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; if `total_net < 0`, verdict becomes `SAFE`. Example from the implementation: a patch that adds 3 new pyright errors but removes 5 ruff warnings yields `total_net = -2`, so it is marked SAFE despite introducing new type errors. That contradicts the docstring above it: “SAFE: no new issues introduced.” 
FOLLOW: This is not just scoring semantics; it crosses the verification boundary. `evaluate_fix()` feeds this verdict to `evaluate_fixes()`, and `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` treats `SAFE` or `NEUTRAL` as sufficient to set `finding.verified = True`. A fix that regresses type safety or security can therefore be programmatically “verified,” causing later NK/bug-closed logic to suppress rediscovery of the bug. That produces silently wrong registry state for the PoC.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute harmfulness per tool/category, not by summed net. If any of `net_type_errors`, `net_ruff_errors`, or `net_bandit_issues` is positive, return `HARMFUL`; only return `SAFE` when at least one net is negative and none are positive.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.76
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can select the wrong source file by substring matching: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. If a finding mentions a basename or partial path like `brain.py`, any source path containing that fragment can match first, regardless of whether it is the intended file. The function also searches both `finding.description` and `finding.proposed_fix`, so incidental file mentions inside fix text can redirect evaluation. This is especially unsafe in a multi-module bench with similarly named files and package paths.
FOLLOW: `evaluate_fix()` then reads, patches, and analyzes the wrong file while reporting `original_file` as that selected path. The sandbox verdict becomes detached from the finding it is supposed to verify. Downstream, a wrong-file SAFE/NEUTRAL can mark the original finding `verified=True` in the immune pipeline, closing the actual bug without ever patching its file. This is an interface-corruption bug between endocrine and immune verification.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require an unambiguous match: first prefer exact normalized path matches against `source_paths`, then unique basename matches, and if multiple candidates match, return `None` so the evaluation becomes `UNEVALUABLE` instead of patching an arbitrary file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.72
FLAW_CLASS: 4
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.48
DESCRIPTION: FIND — the claimed “fix evaluation” tool stack is incomplete in implementation: pre/post counts use only `run_pyright`, `run_ruff`, and `run_bandit`; `run_mypy()` exists but is never used in `evaluate_fix()`, and CrossHair is declared but entirely unused. This matters because the module header and `FixEvaluation` role description present fix evaluation as the “key new capability” for checking whether a proposed fix breaks anything, but one available type checker is ignored during that decision.
FOLLOW: A patch can worsen mypy-visible type correctness while still receiving `SAFE`/`NEUTRAL`, because those regressions are invisible to the verdict computation. Since the immune pipeline trusts SAFE/NEUTRAL to set `verified=True`, this creates another path for false closure of bad fixes. For PoC, this is medium-high because it directly affects correctness of the advertised verifier, not polish.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — include mypy in the pre/post fix-evaluation counts and verdict computation alongside pyright/ruff/bandit; leave CrossHair out for now unless it is actually wired.
VERIFIED: TRUE
